title.narrative: Activity under preparation NaturAfrica phase II

description.narrative: The Action will mainly support the continuation and consolidation of NaturAfrica, the EU¿s Global Gateway flagship regional programme for biodiversity conservation in sub-Saharan Africa launched in 2022, with a second contribution. The overall objective remains to combat biodiversity loss while sustainably improving the livelihoods of local communities living around protected areas, building on the recommendations of the European Commission¿s publication ¿Larger than Elephants¿ for a strategic approach to wildlife conservation in Africa. To achieve this, NaturAfrica phase II will build and consolidate on actions launched during phase I since 2023, in 26 priority transboundary Key Landscapes for Conservation and Development (KLCD), located in six regions, representatives of main African habitats: the West African Sudano-Sahelian savannahs, the West African forests, the Congo basin rainforest, the Transhumance landscapes of Central Africa, the Eastern Rift Savannahs and Watersheds, the Trans-frontier Conservation Areas of Southern Africa. These landscapes cover the continent¿s main ecosystems, which preserve exceptional biodiversity and also provide a basis for sustainable livelihoods for more than 77.7 million people.NaturAfrica phase 2 pursues two closely linked specific objectives: (i) at local/landscape level, to improve ecosystem conservation and the governance of land and natural resources, and promote a green and sustainable economy benefitting local populations, including women and vulnerable groups; (ii) at continental and regional level, to strengthen inclusive governance of transboundary landscapes through cross-border and cross regional cooperation, information sharing, and harmonisation of policies between neighbouring countries. By financing the conservation and restoration of natural habitats and ecosystems, as well as supporting sustainable landscape development, the EU seeks to enhance ecosystem services ¿including carbon sequestration, soil fertility, water regulation, and disaster risk reduction¿while generating tangible benefits for local communities. By the end of Phase 2, NaturAfrica will strengthen the conservation status of at least 26 biodiversity-rich landscapes across 3.4 million km² through improved management and reduced pressures such as deforestation, poaching, and habitat loss. Thousands of households are expected to gain improved access to income-generating opportunities linked to sustainable value chains such as ecotourism, agroforestry, non-timber forest products, and renewable energy. Efforts will also focus on strenghtening inclusive governance, promoting cross-border cooperation, and enhancing participation of women and youth, and local communities in natural resource management, while applying human rights principles in practice. Regional and continental organisations will be supported to play stronger coordination and policy roles, contributing to the continuity and scaling-up of NaturAfrica results beyond the EU funding horizon.
